hero.headline: Garage Door Cable Repair in Aurora, IL

intro: A broken garage door cable needs immediate attention. Your door might hang crooked, make grinding noises, or drop too quickly. These issues prevent safe operation. Our family-owned company repairs garage door cables in Aurora, IL. We serve homes across Kane County, from the Victorian properties near the Fox River to the attached three-car garages in newer subdivisions like Stonebridge. We provide upfront, flat-rate quotes before any work begins. Our service trucks are stocked with common parts. This allows us to complete most repairs in one visit. We are available for dispatch 24 hours Monday through Saturday. Book online for a 10% discount on your repair.
localContext: Aurora's diverse housing stock faces unique challenges. Victorian-era homes with detached garages near the Fox River experience significant humidity swings. This climate can cause older wood doors to warp, putting stress on lift cables. Cables can rust faster when exposed to moisture. Many east-side subdivisions, like Fox Valley, were built in the 1990s–2000s. Their original garage door springs and cables are now reaching end-of-life together. Cables fray or snap over time from normal use. This is especially true for heavier doors on attached three-car garages. Residents in areas like Pigeon Hill might also see issues with cables wrapping off drums due to wear or impact.

problemSigns.sign: Door hangs crooked in the opening
problemSigns.detail: One side of your garage door sits lower than the other, creating an uneven gap.

problemSigns.sign: Cable hanging loose or wrapped off the drum
problemSigns.detail: You see a cable dangling freely or incorrectly spooled on the cable drum above the door.

problemSigns.sign: Grinding noise as the door moves
problemSigns.detail: Unusual scraping or grating sounds indicate a problem with the cable system during door operation.

problemSigns.sign: Door slams down faster than normal
problemSigns.detail: The garage door drops quickly and uncontrolled when closing, indicating a loss of tension from a faulty cable.

process.description: Our technician inspects the garage door system to identify the cause of the cable failure. We check the cables, drums, and bottom brackets.
We give you a flat-rate price for the repair. This quote includes all parts and labor. No hidden fees.
We install new galvanized aircraft-grade lift cables and replace any damaged drums or bottom brackets. Our trucks carry common parts.
After the repair, we perform a balance test and safety-reverse test. This ensures your garage door operates safely and correctly.
